text: Day {n}. The sun came up on schedule. It's the only thing that did.
No new notifications. There won't be.
The shelter smells of canned peaches and unresolved arguments.
Somewhere, a calendar app is still reminding someone about the dentist.
They're gone. The shelter got quieter, and nobody wanted that.
They didn't come back. Their spot by the radio stays empty a while.
Their phone is still at four percent, waiting.
We lost one today. The jokes can wait until tomorrow.
The axe handle snapped. It went down swinging, as advertised.
The flashlight flickered, weighed its options, and chose darkness.
The padlock gave out. It's just door jewellery now.
The radio's last words were a mattress commercial.
Back with supplies, and only a mild glow.
Everyone ate today. Write it down; it may be a record.
The plan worked. Nobody knows what to do with this feeling.
House meeting. Someone has written HOUSE RULES on the wall and underlined it twice.
Another house meeting. The agenda is one line long.
The family gathers at the rules wall. There is room for one more line.
The meeting starts with a cough and a marker pen. Nobody makes eye contact.
Time to decide what kind of shelter this is going to be.
The rules wall is getting crowded. Somebody brought a smaller marker.
One more meeting. The family has learned to vote without looking up.
The neighbour's house has gone quiet. Nobody mentions the medicine.
No lights at the neighbour's house tonight. Or last night.
The house down the street is quiet now. So is the family.
